transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. 

Um... well, I guess I came in because... I’ve just been having a little trouble bouncing back lately? I mean, I know everyone gets sad, but I just can’t seem to shake this... this really heavy, hopeless feeling. It's, um... it's almost like everything I worked so hard to build after my divorce has just sort of collapsed, and I’m just sitting under it. 

I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic, I'm sorry. Am I explaining that okay?
Can you tell me how long you've been feeling this heavy, hopeless way—did it start suddenly, or has it been building up over weeks or months?

Um, well... I guess it’s been about a month now? I really tried to just push through it at first, because I didn't want to overreact or, you know, be a burden to anyone. But it sort of started around... well, there was a bit of a financial mess right after my divorce. 

It's actually a little embarrassing to admit that I let the money stuff get to me so much, but I think that's when this feeling really started hanging over me. It just sort of built up from there. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Over this past month, have you noticed that you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest in everything. I mean, I still try to keep up with things, you know? I don't want to just sit around and do nothing. 

But I guess... maybe things just don't feel quite as fun as they usually do? Like, I used to really enjoy working in my garden on the weekends, and lately it just feels a bit more like a chore. I still do it, of course, because I want it to look nice, but... I don't know, the spark just isn't really there right now. 

Is that the kind of thing you mean? I'm sorry, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. I'm sure it's just a phase.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks of feeling this down or hopeless—at any other point in your life, even before the divorce?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I've had times where I felt a little stressed or overwhelmed, like during finals in college or big projects at work, but... nothing quite like this. 

I've always been pretty good at just putting my head down and getting through things, you know? So I don't think I've ever felt quite this... stuck... before. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture. I really don't think I've ever let things get to me this much in the past.
Over this past month, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, waking up frequently, or sleeping much more than usual?

Um, well... I guess my sleep hasn't been the greatest lately, but I'm sure that's normal when you're stressed, right? I really don't want to complain too much about it. 

But, um... yeah, sometimes I just lie awake staring at the ceiling. My mind just keeps replaying all the bills I have to pay, or little mistakes I made at work. I try to just close my eyes and breathe, but it's hard to turn my brain off. And then, even when I do fall asleep, I've been waking up way before dawn... and I just feel like I didn't actually sleep at all. 

I'm probably just letting the stress get to me too much, honestly. I should probably just try drinking some chamomile tea or something before bed. Does that sound like a normal reaction to stress to you? I hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing.
Over this past month, have you found yourself feeling unusually worthless, or blaming yourself excessively for things that aren't really your fault?

Um... well... I don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or anything. I know everyone makes mistakes and has regrets, especially when going through a divorce. 

But... I guess I have been a little hard on myself lately. It's just... I keep telling myself I'm a terrible engineer, and a failed wife, and... just a burden to everyone around me. It's silly, I know. But I catch myself replaying every little missed calculation at work, or every tense email I've sent, and in my head, it just feels like... like proof that I just ruin things. 

I'm really trying to snap out of it, though. I know I shouldn't think that way. Is it... is it normal to be this hard on yourself when you're stressed? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting.
Have these feelings and low energy made it harder for you to keep up with your job or your daily responsibilities at home?

Um... well... I really try my best to keep everything together, I promise. I hate letting people down, especially at work. But... I guess things have been a little bumpy lately. I was, um, maybe making some questionable calls on a few projects, and I started kind of... falling apart during our team meetings. My supervisor actually had to step in and take me off active project decisions for a bit. I know they were just trying to help, but I feel terrible about being a burden to the firm. I hope I don't sound like a completely incompetent engineer? 

And at home... well, I've sort of let my basic routines slip. Just letting things pile up, which really isn't like me at all. But... um... I guess it got a little worse than just ignoring the laundry. I haven't really wanted to say this because it's just so embarrassing, but... I actually ended up being sent to the emergency department recently. I just... I didn't feel safe with my own thoughts anymore, and things just got out of hand. 

It's so shameful to admit that out loud. I'm really trying to get back on track, though, and do whatever I need to do to fix this. Do you think... do you think it's possible to get past this? I just want to be a reliable person again, if that makes sense.

During this really difficult time, have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, seeing things that weren't there, or having strong beliefs—like feeling you were being punished or that something terrible was going to happen—that others told you weren't true?

Um, no... no, definitely nothing like that. I know my mind has been in a really dark place, and I've been so overwhelmed, but... I haven't heard or seen anything that wasn't there. And I haven't had any, um, strange beliefs or anything. 

I know I've been struggling a lot with feeling guilty and just... down on myself, but I always knew it was just my own thoughts, you know? Just me being too hard on myself. I would never want you to think I was losing touch with reality or anything like that. That would be really scary. 

I'm just dealing with regular stress and sadness, I think. That's... that's a good sign, right? That I'm still thinking clearly, even if I've been feeling so low?
